t.1.77.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Yayāti, having reached his own city, which resembled the city of great Indra, entered the inner apartments and there installed Devayānī.
t.1.77.2: And with Devayānī's consent, he had a house built near the aśoka grove and settled there that daughter of Vṛṣaparvan.
t.1.77.4: Together with Devayānī, that king, the son of Nahuṣa, sported for many years like a god, exceedingly delighted.
t.1.77.3: Śarmiṣṭhā, the daughter of the Asura, surrounded by a thousand slave women, he provided with a share of clothes, food and drink, and treated her with great honor.
t.1.77.5: When her fertile season arrived, Devayānī, that most excellent of women, conceived first, and she gave birth to a son.
t.1.77.6: When a thousand years had passed, Śarmiṣṭhā, the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan, having reached youth, saw her season come, and she reflected.
t.1.77.7: My fertile season has arrived, and yet no husband has been chosen by me. What has befallen me, what now should be done, or by doing what would the right thing be done?
t.1.77.9: "The fruit of a son must be granted to me by the king": such is my firm resolve. Might that righteous-souled one now come to see me in private?
t.1.77.8: Devayānī there has borne a child, while I, though I have reached my youth, remain so in vain. Just as the husband was chosen by her, so too do I choose him.
t.1.77.10: Then that king, having gone out at that time by chance, came upon Śarmiṣṭhā near the aśoka grove and stood there.
t.1.77.11: Seeing him alone in a secluded place, sweetly smiling Śarmiṣṭhā went forward to meet him, joined her palms in reverence, and spoke these words to the king.
t.1.77.13: For you, O king, have always known me by my beauty, my lineage and my conduct; having sought your favour, I beg you: grant me my season, O lord of men.
t.1.77.12: In the family of Soma, of Indra, of Viṣṇu, of Yama, or of Varuṇa, or in your own, O Nāhuṣa, who would presume to touch a woman?
t.1.77.14: Yayāti said: I know you to be a blameless daughter of the Daityas, endowed with good character; and in your beauty I do not see a blemish even the size of a needle's point.
t.1.77.15: When I wed Devayānī, Uśanas Kāvya said: "This daughter of Vṛṣaparvan is not to be summoned by you to your bed."
t.1.77.16: A word spoken in jest does no harm, O king, nor one spoken to women, nor at the time of marriage, nor when life is in danger, nor when all one's wealth is being taken away; these five falsehoods, they say, are not sins.
t.1.77.18: A king is the standard for all beings; he would perish if he spoke falsely. Even if I meet with grave hardship, I cannot bring myself to act falsely.
t.1.77.17: But one who, questioned as a witness, speaks otherwise, O lord of men, they call a man founded on falsehood; and when a common purpose has been agreed upon, the untruth destroys the one who speaks falsely.
t.1.77.19: These two are considered equal, O king: one's own husband and the man who is a friend's husband. They call it the same marriage; you have been chosen as husband by my friend.
t.1.77.20: Yayāti said: "'One must give to those who ask' — this is the vow I have taken. And you ask a wish of me; tell me, what shall I do for you?"
t.1.77.21: Save me from unrighteousness, O king, and establish what is righteous. Having obtained offspring from you, may I practise the highest dharma in the world.
t.1.77.22: Three, O king, are without property of their own: a wife, a slave, and a son; whatever wealth they acquire belongs to the one to whom they belong.
t.1.77.24: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, the king recognized that this was indeed the truth; he honored Śarmiṣṭhā and fulfilled the dharma.
t.1.77.23: I am the servant of Devayānī, and the Bhārgavī is subject to you. Both she and I are to be supported by you, O king; take me to you.
t.1.77.25: Having come together with Śarmiṣṭhā and obtained what they desired, the two honored each other and went back the way they had come.
t.1.77.26: In that union, the fair-browed Śarmiṣṭhā of the charming smile first conceived a child from that best of kings.
t.1.77.27: And then, O king, in due time the lotus-eyed woman gave birth to a boy who shone like a child of the gods, with eyes like lotuses.
